provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Highest budgets in the family and more prospects already have a site, so several openers target dated sites and the design process. No grill, appliance or paver brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Outdoor kitchen layouts and appliance planning
pageStructurePlus.contains: Straight runs, L-shapes and islands with bar seating, grill and side burner placement, sink and fridge, landing space, and venting a grill under a roof
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers arrive with a picture from a magazine and no idea what fits. A layout page turns the dream into a scope they can approve.

pageStructurePlus.section: Gas, water, power and the permit
pageStructurePlus.contains: Running a gas line, trenching for water and drain, outdoor-rated outlets and lighting circuits, which licensed trades do which part, and who pulls the permit
pageStructurePlus.why: Utilities are where outdoor kitchen budgets surprise people. Explaining the coordination up front is what makes a builder look trustworthy.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The site visit, measured plan, rendered views of the patio and kitchen, revision rounds, the design fee, and how it credits toward the build
pageStructurePlus.why: High-ticket buyers commit to a design process before they commit to a build. Showing the steps gets the paid consult booked.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Excavation depth, compacted base, bedding sand, edge restraint, joint sand, slope away from the house, and why patios heave or sink
pageStructurePlus.why: Hardscape buyers have seen neighbours' pavers sink. Showing the base explains the price gap between quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Phase one patio and walls, phase two kitchen and seating wall, phase three fire feature and lighting, with utilities stubbed in early for later phases
pageStructurePlus.why: Many buyers can't do it all in one season. A phased plan keeps them with one hardscaper for years.

designDirections.name: Patio First
designDirections.bestFor: Paver and hardscape crews moving into their first outdoor kitchen projects
designDirections.headlineSample: Paver patios and outdoor kitchens in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Cacao browns sit beside stone and stained wood, and the bookish serif keeps a smaller crew looking established without overselling.

designDirections.name: Built Outside
designDirections.bestFor: Design-build hardscapers with a backlog of finished kitchens, seating walls and paver patios
designDirections.headlineSample: Outdoor kitchens and hardscape built in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo. Brick red and linen match stone veneer and pavers, and slab headings feel like a mason's mark on a project board.

designDirections.name: Evening Terrace
designDirections.bestFor: High-end outdoor living builders selling full backyard kitchens with fireplaces and covered bars
designDirections.whyItFits: A midnight ground with champagne accents shows kitchens at dusk, lights on, and the Didone display reads as custom work with a design fee.

openers.line: For a company building outdoor kitchens at your level, it surprised me that {Business Name} has no site on its listing. Someone spending that kind of money wants to study your hardscape work before the first call.
openers.hook: Open their listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a serious outdoor kitchen buyer would find instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing points to Facebook, where a finished outdoor kitchen with a stone bar sits next to a post about a skid steer. A buyer planning a big backyard needs a project page, not a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their listing link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the most recent kitchen or patio they posted.
openers.linkLine: Your outdoor kitchens on a page built for buyers: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site talks about pavers and walls but has no outdoor kitchen projects on it, even though your Instagram is full of them. The highest-ticket work you do is invisible to anyone searching.
openers.hook: Compare their site's gallery with their Instagram grid. If kitchens appear only on social, use this.
openers.linkLine: Your outdoor kitchens with their own project pages: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone your hardscape gallery opens each patio as a tiny thumbnail that won't enlarge. People planning an outdoor kitchen scroll projects on the couch for weeks.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your hardscape gallery, working on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way on your profile to book a design consult for an outdoor kitchen, only a phone number. Buyers at this budget want to send the yard size, the wish list and a rough budget first.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for a consult or project form. If calling is the only path, use this.
openers.linkLine: A design consult request that asks layout, budget and timeline: {demo-link}

openers.line: The stone-clad kitchen island with the pizza oven and the covered bar on your grid are portfolio pieces. Right now they're buried under equipment and jobsite posts.
openers.hook: Find two finished outdoor kitchens on their grid you can describe by feature. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your outdoor kitchens, each with its own project page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews describe a backyard that became where the family eats all summer and a crew that kept the build on schedule. That's the reassurance a big hardscape buyer needs, and it's stuck on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about a kitchen, patio or the build experience. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the backyards they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Outdoor kitchens that get cooked on by Memorial Day were designed in the cold months. The hardscapers that buyers find in January are the ones whose spring is already sold.
openers.hook: Use from November to February. Name the season and their usual lead time if they post it.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the winter design season: {demo-link}

openers.line: Couples plan an outdoor kitchen at the table after dinner, phones out, comparing builders. If the only option is calling in the morning, the one with a consult form gets the first meeting.
openers.hook: Call the listed number after hours. If it hits a generic or full voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A consult request that works after dinner: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a mason for your hardscape crew. Skilled stone setters choose the company with the best work on display.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: A hardscape company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your projects run into the bigger-lot towns around {City}, but nothing tells a homeowner in {Neighborhood} you build outdoor kitchens there. That's the search with the most money behind it.
openers.hook: Collect the towns from their project captions and reviews, and use the most affluent one they name.
openers.linkLine: An outdoor kitchen page for each town you build in: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you finance outdoor kitchens or offer phased payments, that belongs beside the design consult form. At this budget most families plan the payments first.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing publicly. If not, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Outdoor kitchen financing explained up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: An outdoor kitchen means a gas line, a circuit and a permit. Showing your licence, insurance and the licensed trades you bring in answers the question a careful buyer has before anything else.
openers.hook: Check the state registry for a contractor record. Never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, trades and permits on one outdoor kitchen page: {demo-link}

openers.line: I'd guess a lot of your outdoor kitchen work comes through designers, pool builders and past clients. Each of those referrals still searches {Business Name} before the first meeting.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or tags mentioning a designer, pool builder or 'referred by'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a designer's referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you finished is the kind of outdoor kitchen people plan a whole summer around. It should open your portfolio, not drift down a feed.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished kitchen or patio and name its features: island, bar, oven, cover, the town if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That outdoor kitchen, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} is serious outdoor kitchen work.

I was looking at hardscape builders in {City} and found {Business Name} on Instagram and Maps, but nowhere a buyer can study your kitchens project by project and book a design consult. I built a sample site to show the idea, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Should I send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample outdoor kitchen and hardscape site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

Each kitchen gets its own project page, there's a design consult request that asks layout and budget, and a page on gas, power and permits. If it's not a fit, say so and I'll step back.
sequence.call:
"Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for outdoor kitchen and hardscape companies in {City}. I sent a note about a sample site for {Business Name}. Did you get a chance to see it?"

IF NO:
"No problem. It's a sample site with each outdoor kitchen on its own project page, a design consult request, and a utilities and permits page, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What stood out, good or bad?"
 → listen, then ask how most of their kitchen jobs start today
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many project pages and towns you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and updates. For your work I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is less than the stone veneer on one island."
"Can we look at it together for fifteen minutes this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send the scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before the winter design season gets busy."

objections.handler: "You do, and it covers pavers. Your outdoor kitchens, the highest-ticket thing you build, aren't on it. The sample shows what it looks like when they are."

objections.objection: Our work comes from designers and builders.
objections.handler: "Those referrals are the best you'll get. Every one of them still looks you up before the meeting. Project pages make that look match the price."

objections.objection: I've been burned by an agency before.
objections.handler: "Fair. That's why you've already seen the sample before paying anything. One-page scope, fixed price, and the domain stays in your name."

objections.objection: We're booked out through next season.
objections.handler: "Then the site's job is to raise the average ticket, not fill the calendar. A consult form that asks budget up front lets you pick the full-backyard projects."
"Good, I'm happy to work with them. I'd build the project pages and consult form; they keep the look and the posts."
"{Build Range}. For you, around {Build Price}: kitchen project pages, a design consult form, a utilities and permits page and town pages. Less than one island's countertop."

email.subject: Outdoor kitchen site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for outdoor kitchen builders in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll email the link so you can look tonight. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm archiving the {Business Name} outdoor kitchen demo on Friday.

Shall I hold it for you a while longer? One word either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, design season for spring outdoor kitchens is starting and the consult requests come with it. Thought of {Business Name}.

The sample site is still up and the price is the same: {demo-link}

bullets: Price by project page, not by page count. A high-ticket hardscaper sells one finished outdoor kitchen at a time, each with its own story.
The design consult request with budget and timeline fields is the most valuable piece. Charge for it as its own line.
Expect more revision rounds than smaller trades; build a review round into every quote.
Peg the build against the countertop or veneer on one kitchen island, never against hours.
Include the utilities and permits page only when the builder coordinates gas and electrical; leave it out for patio-only crews.
Quote video walkthroughs only for builders with finished kitchens they can film at dusk.

lineItems.description: Max with a written story, before-and-after pairs, a feature list and a short dusk video clip.

lineItems.item: Design consult request with budget and layout
lineItems.description: Max with picture upload, a wish-list checklist, budget bands, phase options and routing to the designer.
Max when it covers several towns' permit steps and explains each trade the builder coordinates.
Max with three worked phase examples and utilities stub-out notes.
Max when each town page carries its own finished kitchens and local permit notes.

lineItems.item: Rendering gallery from past design consults
lineItems.description: Max when renderings are paired with the finished build for the same backyard.
Max for a narrated walk through two or three kitchens with captions and chapter marks.

whatElseYouSell.name: Dusk outdoor kitchen photo and video shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One evening at your best outdoor kitchen with the bar lights and the fire on, stills and a short walkthrough. That shoot sells the next six-figure backyard."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on the next finished kitchen the owners will let you shoot.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile project posts for hardscape
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A finished kitchen, wall or patio goes onto your Maps profile every week with the town and the features named."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks at the first cookout
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Two weeks after handover, when they've hosted the first cookout on the new patio, the client gets a note asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Printed outdoor kitchen lookbook
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed lookbook of your best kitchens to leave on the table after a design consult. Buyers at this budget show it to each other."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there are enough project pages to pull from.

whatElseYouSell.name: Winter design-consult campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A January campaign aimed at bigger-lot neighbourhoods books design consults for spring builds before other hardscapers return calls."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run December through February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite banners and trailer wrap
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "An outdoor kitchen build runs for weeks in a visible backyard. A fence banner and a wrapped trailer turn that into calls from the street."

whatElseYouSell.name: Designer and architect partner page
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A page for landscape architects and designers showing how you build their hardscape drawings, with a trade contact form."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if designers already send them work.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring open-house event at a finished backyard
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A past client hosts an evening at their outdoor kitchen, you invite prospects through the site, and the kitchen does the selling."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 6, in spring, with a happy past client.

withoutAI.whoPays: The stone and hardscape supply yard
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The yard where you buy veneer and pavers has a showroom and a site that hasn't changed in years. Introduce me and I'll build their contractor gallery."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply yards sell to every hardscaper around and want to show finished work made from their stone.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The showroom where your clients pick their grill heads sends them to builders. A site that shows appliances in real outdoor kitchens sells more of both."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dealer and builder share every customer; the builder's finished kitchens are the dealer's best content.

withoutAI.route: Licensed plumbers and electricians on kitchen jobs
withoutAI.whoPays: The trade contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The plumber who runs your gas lines and the electrician who wires the island need sites too. One word from you is enough."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: These trades rarely market themselves and trust the hardscaper who gives them steady work.

withoutAI.whoPays: The pool builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pool builder whose decks meet your patios has the same high-ticket buyer. Introduce me and both sites link to each other."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pool and kitchen projects are sold to the same family in the same season.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The designer whose plans you build needs a portfolio site that shows the finished backyards, not just the drawings."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers need built proof and the hardscaper has it. The intro comes from a trusted partner.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every finished outdoor kitchen needs bar stools and a dining set. The local furniture shop needs a site that shows its pieces in real backyards."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same buyer, the month after the build. The hardscaper's projects make the retailer's site credible.

withAI.route: Stone quantity assistant for the supply yard
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors describe the wall or island and the assistant drafts the veneer, cap and paver quantities, priced from that yard."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps contractors ordering from one yard and cuts counter time.

withAI.route: Appliance fit checker for the grill showroom
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers enter the island length and the assistant suggests which grill, burner and fridge combinations fit, with cut-out sizes for the builder."
withAI.whyItWorks: Wrong cut-outs cause returns and angry builders. The dealer pays to prevent them.

withAI.route: Design brief intake for landscape architects
withAI.pitchLine: "Clients answer a guided set of questions about how they use the yard, and the studio gets a tidy design brief before the first meeting."
withAI.whyItWorks: Designers spend the first meeting gathering basics. The hardscaper introduced you.

withAI.pitchLine: "Pool buyers ask about patios and kitchens around the pool at night. An assistant answers from both companies' scopes and books a joint consult."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells bigger joint projects and the pool builder sees it working for a partner.

withAI.route: Furniture layout preview for the patio retailer
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers upload their new patio and see furniture sets placed to scale before they buy."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells larger sets, and the hardscaper's finished patios are the demo material.

withAI.route: HOA architectural review pre-check for hardscape
withAI.pitchLine: "Outdoor kitchen and patio submissions get checked against the HOA's setback, height and material rules before the committee sees them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Committees meet monthly and every resubmission delays a build. The manager pays for fewer rounds.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for hardscape enquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls you miss while setting stone get a text asking whether it's a patio, a wall or an outdoor kitchen, and when they want it done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and the wording approved.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for outdoor kitchen projects
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New reviews get a reply drafted that names the kitchen or patio and the family's first cookout, ready for your approval."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies to match their voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Outdoor kitchen budget builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Buyers pick island size, finish level, appliances and a patio area and see a realistic range, so the design consult starts from a real budget."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price bands by finish level, appliance allowances and patio prices per square foot.

softwareAI.name: Design fee and milestone billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Design fee at booking, deposit at contract, draws at base, at kitchen framing and at completion, each invoiced automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their milestone schedule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Consult brief summariser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The consult form, the yard pictures and the budget come back as a one-page brief, so you walk into the outdoor kitchen meeting prepared."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the consult form live and their brief template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Project board from consult to handover
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every hardscape job from design fee to permit, base, utilities, kitchen and punch list on one board, with each trade's dates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their stages and the trades they schedule.

softwareAI.name: Outdoor kitchen concept visualiser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From a yard picture and the wish list it drafts two labelled concept views of the kitchen and patio, so the first meeting starts with something to react to."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a set of their finished kitchens and their standard layouts. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Trade scheduling texts for gas and electrical
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the base is done, the plumber and electrician get a text with the address and the trench date, and the client gets a heads-up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the project board and their trades' contacts.

softwareAI.name: Client portal with design approvals and selections
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients approve renderings, pick stone, countertop and appliances, and see the build schedule in one place instead of thirty texts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the project board in place first.

softwareAI.name: After-hours consult booking assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers evening calls, asks about the outdoor kitchen they have in mind and their budget band, and books a paid design consult."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar, consult fee and screening questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Selections and allowance tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tracks each client's appliance, stone and countertop picks against the allowance, so overages are signed before ordering."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their allowance rules and supplier lists.

softwareAI.name: Hardscape chatbot on layouts, utilities and lead times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can I put a grill under my patio cover' and 'when could you start' at midnight, from your own guidance and schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their layout and utility notes and current lead time. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Estimate builder with stone and paver takeoff
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the patio area, wall lengths and island size, and it produces the estimate and the material list for the yard order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their unit prices, waste factors and estimate template.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to scope for the site walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the backyard on the site walk and it drafts the hardscape scope: patio size, kitchen run, utilities and access."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their scope template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Annual outdoor kitchen care visit sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each spring, past clients get a reminder for a kitchen check: sealing stone, re-sanding joints and servicing the grill. That's paid work from every build you've done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a list of past builds with dates and the care visit price.

softwareAI.name: Project story writer for kitchen pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From your job notes and a five-minute voice memo, it drafts the project page for each finished outdoor kitchen for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their notes and sign-off on each page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by phase and trade
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See margin by patio, wall and kitchen phase once stone, appliances, subs and crew days are in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of invoices, sub bills and crew days.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with base and utility sleeve checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Crews log base depth, compaction, gas sleeves and conduit with pictures before anything gets buried under the patio."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, with two or more crews. Needs their checklist and a foreman to pilot.

softwareAI.name: Approved-design material list generator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Once the design is approved, the block, veneer, cap and countertop quantities for the hardscape order come straight from its dimensions."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs their unit rules per wall and island type and a few past real material lists to check against.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for masons and hardscape crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for mason and paver crew roles answer the questions you always ask, and you only meet the ones who can actually set stone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs their must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Outdoor kitchen budget builder as a subscription
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Hardscape and outdoor living companies, monthly
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The outdoor kitchen budget builder that made one company's consults easier works for every hardscaper whose buyers show up with no number in mind."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the logic. Other builders load their own price bands.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Contractor locator for a paver and wall block manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who like your pavers want a certified hardscape contractor nearby. A locator with project galleries sends them to your installers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund contractor programs, and the hardscape client proves you know the trade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every dealer in your network gets a page of outdoor kitchens built with your appliances by local builders."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want dealers selling more islands. Real builds are the strongest content they can offer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A hardscape template with project pages, a consult form and a utilities page, offered to every member company."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need member benefits, and one deal reaches many owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency white-label for outdoor living clients
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with outdoor kitchen clients rebuild project pages and consult forms each time. License the finished hardscape template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the client; you supply the finished trade-specific build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each outdoor kitchen territory needs project pages, a consult form and town pages routed to its owner. One build, many territories."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One agreement becomes many locations on one template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Luxury home builder outdoor options studio
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Custom home buyers choose an outdoor kitchen package during design. An options studio page sells it and hands it to one hardscaper."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders want upgrade revenue and a reliable partner. The hardscape client becomes the default.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Showroom display partnerships for supply yards
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your showroom has a display kitchen nobody can see online. A virtual tour with builder credits brings buyers in and sends them to your contractors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Supply yards spend on showroom traffic, and the hardscaper built half of what's on display.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short note on where stone, countertop and appliance allowances are moving, built only from invoices hardscapers share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders set allowances months ahead; shared data keeps the note grounded.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Clubs and venues with an outdoor kitchen or terrace need an events page that shows it off, and your client built it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Commercial owners have bigger budgets and the hardscaper already has the relationship.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One outdoor kitchen builder per metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A hardscape builder in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I take one outdoor kitchen builder per metro so project pages and the budget builder stay exclusive. Your metro is spoken for; the next isn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive territory lets you reuse everything and sell exclusivity as a feature.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "If your agency left you with a site you can't update, I can move your outdoor kitchen projects onto a template that's already working for another builder."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already value a site; they want someone dependable.

upsellLadder.offer: Outdoor kitchen site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The outdoor kitchen site and the care plan go on one contract, so each new project page is a message to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks and Google profile project posts
upsellLadder.trigger: A client hosts the first cookout on a kitchen finished since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "They've had the first cookout. That's the moment to ask for the review and post the kitchen."

upsellLadder.offer: Dusk outdoor kitchen photo and video shoot
upsellLadder.trigger: A finished kitchen the owners are happy to show, or project pages still using placeholders.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot that kitchen at dusk with the lights on. It becomes the first thing every buyer sees."

upsellLadder.trigger: Consult requests show buyers arriving without a budget, or consults that end at the first number.
upsellLadder.line: "Those consults that ended at the first number are what this fixes. Buyers arrive already knowing the range."

upsellLadder.trigger: More than a handful of consult requests a month with yard pictures uploaded by buyers.
upsellLadder.line: "You're getting enough outdoor kitchen consults that a one-page brief before each saves real prep time."

upsellLadder.offer: Project board from consult to handover
upsellLadder.trigger: A trade shows up on the wrong day, or they start running two builds at once.
upsellLadder.line: "That missed plumber day is a scheduling problem. One board with every hardscape trade's dates fixes it."

upsellLadder.offer: Client portal with design approvals and selections
upsellLadder.trigger: A selection mix-up or a client complaining about texts to track decisions.
upsellLadder.line: "After that countertop mix-up, let's put every outdoor kitchen selection and approval in one place the client signs."

upsellLadder.offer: Annual outdoor kitchen care visit sequence
upsellLadder.trigger: The first anniversary of the earliest kitchens built since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "Last year's kitchens are due for sealing and a grill service. Every one is a paid visit and a chance at phase two."
